title: Tagged genesis recovery-incarnation proof
description: Objective: make a never-restored store's genesis fence a canonical self-proving public recovery identity without fabricating restore facts. Deliverable: refactor the landed recovery-incarnation mint/codec around an exact tagged context union (RESTORE with restoreCommandId+backupGenerationDigest; GENESIS with daemon-derived project/store context), preserve the existing restore API, and expose a synchronous or otherwise startup-composable genesis mint that returns full public SPKI/fingerprint/binding digest/signature proof while never serializing the nonce, private key, PKCS8, or handle. This is a prerequisite for task-e19074f841f9450296799abfba9bfcaa; the current genesis helper persists only refs plus a genesisDigest, while RecoveryIncarnationBinding requires restore-only fields that a fresh store does not possess. NOT in scope: SQLite installation/CAS, daemon startup/listener changes, restore quiesce policy, session lifetime, or using the key as signing authority. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run src/recovery/recovery-incarnation.test.ts src/identity/genesis-recovery-binding.test.ts.
definitionOfDone: The public recovery-incarnation contract uses an exact tagged GENESIS versus RESTORE origin; GENESIS cannot carry or counterfeit restoreCommandId/backupGenerationDigest, and RESTORE retains its current exact fields and behavior.

One production mint/verification implementation derives incarnationRef and keyEpochRef from fresh 256-bit entropy, complete Ed25519 SPKI fingerprint, and the tagged context, and returns a full canonical binding/proof whose signature verifies.

Genesis context is derived inside the daemon from the asserted project/store identity, never caller-selected recovery refs, counters, time, or restored bytes; repeated entropy/key material is refused with the existing exact recovery code/layer.

Canonical serialized public evidence contains no raw nonce, private key, PKCS8, key handle, bearer, or proof-of-possession secret; losing/unused key handles are destroyed and the result claims no signing/business authority.

Existing restore-incarnation, succession, anchor, and hostile-input tests remain green; generated GENESIS/RESTORE and mutation sweeps assert nonzero counts and removing either context or SPKI binding reddens focused tests.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck and the focused recovery-incarnation/genesis tests exit 0.
taskRails: Do not synthesize restoreCommandId or backupGenerationDigest for a never-restored store; model genesis as an explicit tagged origin.
Reuse the landed recovery crypto/freshness/self-proof discipline rather than a second generateKeyPairSync implementation.
This task proves only a fencing identity; it must not claim a durable usable signing key or persist/resurrect a private key handle.
Every refusal test asserts the exact stable reason code, layer, and component where exposed; mutation drills exercise the production verifier.

implementationPlan.description: TDD. Create the tagged context union and the ONE shared derivation core. Export: RECOVERY_INCARNATION_ORIGINS = Object.freeze(['GENESIS','RESTORE'] as const) and RecoveryIncarnationOrigin; RestoreIncarnationContext {origin:'RESTORE'; restoreCommandId; backupGenerationDigest}; GenesisIncarnationContext {origin:'GENESIS'; projectId; storeContextDigest}; the union RecoveryIncarnationContext; snapshotRestoreContext(value) and snapshotGenesisContext(value) reusing the existing descriptor-snapshot discipline (exact own-key set, data properties only, refuse extra keys) copied in style from snapshotRequest; contextParts(context) returning the framed derivation parts with the ORIGIN TAG FIRST for BOTH origins ([origin, restoreCommandId, backupGenerationDigest] / [origin, projectId, storeContextDigest]); and deriveIncarnation({context, incarnationDigest, verificationKeyFingerprint, publicKeySpkiHex}) returning frozen {incarnationRef, keyEpochRef, bindingDigest, challengeDigest} using the existing digestOf domains 'incarnation' / 'key-epoch' / 'binding' / 'challenge'. CRITICAL: snapshotGenesisContext must NOT accept a caller-supplied storeContextDigest — it derives it as digestOf('genesis-store', projectId) internally and refuses an object that carries the key at all, because DoD-3 forbids caller-selected context. Import digestOf and RECOVERY_INCARNATION_SCHEMA_VERSION from recovery-incarnation-contract.js; do NOT re-implement framing. Tests in recovery-incarnation.test.ts: assert a GENESIS and a RESTORE context whose raw string parts are deliberately identical derive DIFFERENT incarnationRef/keyEpochRef/bindingDigest (cross-origin collision resistance), and assert snapshotGenesisContext refuses a caller-supplied storeContextDigest.

implementationPlan.description: TDD. Move the durable binding wire codec OUT of recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts into a new focused module and make it origin-aware. Keep the ONE fixed field order property that makes re-anchor idempotent — emit keys in a single deterministic order per origin, never from the caller's object. decodeBinding must refuse: an unknown/missing origin, a GENESIS payload carrying restoreCommandId or backupGenerationDigest, a RESTORE payload carrying projectId or storeContextDigest, and any drifted/truncated/extended row — all by returning null, unchanged in kind from today. implementationPlan.note: New recovery-incarnation-binding-codec.ts (168 lines) + .js bridge holds the wire codec: encodeBinding emits ONE fixed key order per origin (common 10, then the origin's own 2) built from a local literal, never from the caller's object; decodeBinding reads the origin FIRST, selects the exact per-origin key set, and only then reads fields. implementationPlan.description: TDD. Add the startup-composable SYNCHRONOUS genesis mint in a new focused module. Export mintGenesisIncarnation(projectId: string): GenesisMintResult, a discriminated result of {ok:true; outcome:'MINTED'; authority:'NONE'; binding: GenesisIncarnationBinding} or the EXISTING RecoveryIncarnationRefused shape reusing RECOVERY_ENTROPY_UNAVAILABLE / RECOVERY_KEY_EPOCH_UNAVAILABLE at layer RECOVERY_INCARNATION — do not invent new codes. It must be sync: use node:crypto randomBytes, generateKeyPairSync('ed25519'), sign and verify. It MUST call snapshotGenesisContext + deriveIncarnation from step 1, so derivation and self-proof are single-sourced with the async service. Carry over the landed discipline explicitly: a module-level seenNonceDigests Set so repeated entropy is refused with RECOVERY_ENTROPY_UNAVAILABLE; the raw-nonce block reserved before the keypair is generated; the SPKI exported once and copied; a real sign/verify round trip checked with !== true before anything is returned. Per task rail 3 this returns NO key handle at all and the private KeyObject must go out of scope immediately — never stored in a map, never returned, never serialized. Tests in recovery-incarnation.test.ts assert the returned binding's proof verifies against its own publicKeySpkiHex, that origin is 'GENESIS', that a second call with a stubbed repeated nonce is refused with the exact code AND layer, and that JSON.stringify of the binding contains no private key, PKCS8, nonce or handle.

implementationPlan.note: Adversarial pass, seven questions answered by probe not by reading intent. (1) Cross-origin reach: grep for casts across the union in production returns NONE; both mints build literals of their own branch only, and decodeBinding picks the exact key set from the origin BEFORE reading a field. (2) Pre-origin row: refused (drill 3 plus the "refuses a pre-origin row rather than inventing an origin for it" test). I also found and closed a real gap here — nothing pinned that an anchored GENESIS row is not a restore lineage, so recovery-succession.test.ts gained "anchors a GENESIS binding and still reads NO restore incarnation for it": it anchors a real minted genesis binding, asserts hasAnchoredIncarnation is TRUE (so the null is the origin check, not a missing write), readAnchoredIncarnation is null, and readSuccessionChain refuses RECOVERY_PREDECESSOR_NOT_FOUND at layer RECOVERY_SUCCESSION. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
TAGGING SHAPE — the most contestable decision in this plan, flagged for QA. Option A was a nested `context` discriminated union field replacing the two flat fields; the description's phrase 'tagged context union' leans this way. REJECTED because DoD-1 says 'RESTORE retains its current exact fields' and the description says 'preserve the existing restore API', and moving restoreCommandId under a nested object changes the public shape every existing caller reads. CHOSEN: a top-level discriminated union keyed on `origin`, so RESTORE keeps both field names exactly where they are and GENESIS is structurally incapable of carrying them. This satisfies both DoD-1 clauses at once.

DOMAIN SEPARATION — symmetric vs asymmetric. An asymmetric option was available that preserves RESTORE's derived digest VALUES byte-for-byte: leave RESTORE's parts as [restoreCommandId, backupGenerationDigest] untagged and tag only GENESIS. Because digestOf is length-framed and the two origins would have different arities (2 vs 3), that is technically collision-safe today. REJECTED: it is safe only by arity accident, and a future edit adding a third RESTORE part silently opens a collision surface. CHOSEN: tag BOTH origins first. CONSEQUENCE THE WORKER AND QA MUST BOTH KNOW — RESTORE's derived incarnationRef/keyEpochRef values now differ for identical inputs. Fields and behavior are preserved; derived values are not. This is intended and is NOT a DoD-1 violation. Any test pinning a hardcoded ref digest must be changed to derive it.

SCHEMA VERSION — not bumped, deliberately. RECOVERY_INCARNATION_SCHEMA_VERSION is mixed into every digestOf call, so bumping it would change every ref anyway and buys nothing; and a pre-existing anchored row already fails the exact-key check once `origin` is required, which is fail-closed. This is a pre-release epic with no durable rows to honor. If QA disagrees, the fix is a one-line constant change, not a redesign.

ONE MINT IMPLEMENTATION — DoD-2 says 'one production mint/verification implementation'. Since the sync/async split is forced (see codebaseInsights 4), single-sourcing is achieved at the DERIVATION AND SELF-PROOF layer: deriveIncarnation + contextParts + the binding assembly are shared, and the two IO shells differ only in which crypto API they call. A third option — making the mint generic over a sync/async port union — was rejected as over-engineering for this size.

NOT SPLIT VIA SPIDR. Nine distinct files exceeds the 5-file soft guidance and will warn. Splitting was rejected because the union change is atomic: the moment RecoveryIncarnationBinding becomes a union the anchor codec stops typechecking, so contract + codec + anchor + both mints cannot land separately without leaving the daemon red between tasks. Per the epic rail, size is bounded by plan shape (10 steps, 9 files — both under the 12/10 hard thresholds), never by summed LOC.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
ALL CLAIMS BELOW RE-MEASURED AT HEAD d7a71cb, not read off the description.

(1) `ls apps/daemon/src/recovery` + grep: the daemon is at apps/daemon, NOT packages/daemon.

(2) grep RecoveryIncarnationBinding -> recovery-incarnation-contract.ts:68-80 carries FLAT REQUIRED restoreCommandId + backupGenerationDigest and has NO origin discriminator. snapshotRequest pins REQUEST_KEYS=['backupGenerationDigest','restoreCommandId'] with an exact-length refusal, so genesis cannot even be expressed as a request today. Grep for a tagged GENESIS origin in production returns nothing (only an unrelated GENESIS_STATE state-machine node name in packages/testkit/src/schedule/schedule-universe-tables.ts).

(3) THE CENTRAL DEFECT. genesis-recovery-binding.ts mintGenesis computes spki, fingerprint, bindingDigest and signature as LOCALS and returns only {genesisDigest, incarnationRef, keyEpochRef} (line 118). The public key is discarded, so nothing downstream can ever re-verify. The durable ACTIVE payload is literally 64 hex ASCII chars: `payload: encoder.encode(minted.genesisDigest)`. A grep for spki/fingerprint/sign/verify HITS in that file and looks complete — it is not, the proof is ephemeral. Judge availability by the RETURN TYPE and the persisted bytes, never the function body.

(4) THE DESIGN IS FORCED, NOT CHOSEN. createStoreDependencies (daemon-store-dependencies.ts:88) is SYNCHRONOUS and calls ensureGenesisRecoveryBinding at line 98. The landed crypto port createNodeRecoveryCryptoPort (recovery-incarnation.node.ts) is built on webcrypto.subtle, which is ASYNC-ONLY — there is no sync WebCrypto path. Daemon startup changes are explicitly out of scope. Therefore genesis MUST have a sync crypto shell; it cannot reuse the async port. Do not burn an hour discovering this. The description's phrase 'synchronous OR OTHERWISE startup-composable' is what licenses it.

(5) Blast radius of the union: grep -rln RecoveryIncarnationBinding hits index.ts, recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts, recovery-incarnation-contract.ts, recovery-incarnation.ts, recovery-key-provider.ts, recovery-succession.ts, restore-test-harness.ts, packages/store/src/sqlite-schema-recovery-manifest.ts, plus 4 test files. Only the anchor destructures the restore-only fields (lines 43,55,107-127) so only the anchor codec is forced to change; the rest re-export or pass the type through. packages/store's hit is a name-only reference — check it but expect no edit.

(6) Async mint callers: recovery-key-provider.ts:113, recovery-succession.ts:112, restore-test-harness.ts:187. All use `await ...mint({restoreCommandId, backupGenerationDigest})`. Preserving that request API keeps all three untouched.

planningNotes.risks:
CONSUMER EDGE / GLOBAL RAIL CLAUSE 1. This task lands the mint but deliberately does NOT persist the full proof — SQLite installation is out of scope. Naming the consumer tasks as the rail requires: task-69fdb23140ab472ebd34c3e4478c3ef2 (Genesis-aware restore record classification, currently BLOCKED ON THIS TASK) consumes the canonical genesis payload, and task-e19074f841f9450296799abfba9bfcaa (Genesis recovery binding for first-boot authentication) composes it at startup. Until one of those lands, mintGenesisIncarnation's proof is returned and dropped — the defect measured in codebaseInsights 3 SURVIVES this task by design. Say so plainly in complete_task; do not describe this task as having fixed the discarded-proof defect.

DERIVED REF VALUES CHANGE for RESTORE (see approachesConsidered). Expect red in any test that hardcodes a digest. That red is correct and must be fixed by deriving, not by pinning the new constant.

OLD ANCHORED ROWS become undecodable once `origin` is required. Verify this is null-return (absent), never an admitted row with an invented origin — that is adversarial-review item 2 and is the difference between fail-closed and fail-open.

SHARED WORKTREE. Live peers are working in this same directory right now (worker-25ca55c6 and worker-40286572 in packages/runner, architect-8b21d0bb on task-1615065497f0489097a4bbc11cea9d6b which also touches recovery-binding install). git status will show foreign modifications in .moe/** and packages/runner/**. Commit by explicit pathspec only; never git add -A, never a bare git commit. If a foreign whole-tree commit captures your files, report the base-ref diff instead of repairing it.

MUTATION DRILL HAZARDS, all previously observed on this board: a drill that applied nothing reads as green (make the mutation print the replaced range and chain with &&); a drill can redden for the WRONG reason (read the failure message, not the count — over-reddening means a broken env); restoring with git checkout destroys uncommitted work and reverts to HEAD rather than pre-drill bytes (restore with Edit and compare hashes).

TASK RAIL 3 IS EASY TO VIOLATE ACCIDENTALLY. The sync genesis mint must claim no signing authority and must not retain the private key. generateKeyPairSync returns a KeyObject that is structured-cloneable and whose PKCS8 stays exportable while JSON.stringify misleadingly yields {} — it LOOKS contained and is not. Let it die with the call; never put it in a map, a closure, or a returned property.
